Abstract: We report here an indium(III) triflate
(In(OTf)3)-catalyzed Prins-type cyclizationo fd isub-
stituted b-allenols in the presence of aldehydes in di-
chloromethane (CH2Cl2)a ffording different 3,6-dihy-
dro-2H-pyran at room temperature or 45 88C. The
high efficiency of the reactiona nd easily available
nature of the starting materials/catalyst make it
useful in synthesizing different dihydropyran deriva-
tives.A rationale for the formation of all the prod-
ucts was proposed.
Keywords: b-allenols;a ldehydes;i ndium(III) triflate;
Prins reaction; 2H-pyrans
Introduction
Dihydropyran skeletons have been found in many
natural products.[1] Many methodologies have been
developed for the synthesis of dihydropyran deriva-
tives,i ncluding hetero-Diels–Alder[2] and olefin meta-
thesis reactions.[3] TheP rins cyclization is ah ighly effi-
cient approach toward heterocycles under mild reac-
tion conditions.[4,5] Recently,o ur group has reported
the FeCl3-catalyzed cyclization of terminal a- or b-sul-
fonamidoallenes or b-allenenols and aldehydes in the
presence of TMSClt of orm 4-chloro-1,2,3,6-tetrahy-
dropyridines,3 -chloromethyl-2,5-dihydro-1H-pyrroles,
or 1,2,5,6-tetrahydro-1H-pyridines or 5,6-dihydro-2H-
pyrans( Scheme 1).[6] Herein, we report ah ighly effi-
cient In(OTf)3-catalyzedP rins-type cyclization of 5,5-
disubstituted 3,4-allenols anda ldehydes to synthesize
3,6-dihydro-2H-pyrans or 5,6-dihydro-2H-pyrans
(Scheme 1).

In(OTf)3-catalyzed Prins-type cyclization of b-allenols
and aldehydesa ffording 3,6-dihydro-2H-pyrans or
5,6-dihydro-2H-pyrans depending on the reaction
conditions.M echanistic studies confirmed the conver-
sion between these two classes of productsl eading to
ar ationale for their formation. Due to the easily
availability of the starting materials,[9a,11] the high effi-
ciency of the catalyst and the simple operation,t he
